document.title: feat(examples): demo Deck App touring every SDK feature
document.summary: Adds `js/examples/demo`, a Deck App named VitaDeck Demo with one section per SDK feature, a nav column and L/R switching, plus a README and a link from the root README.
document.why: Máté asked to [top everything off with a Demo app showcasing all the VitaDeck features](source:s1).

sources.label: Roadmap thread brief · Oct 25
sources.gist: Build js/examples/demo: one section per SDK feature, Stack/Scroll layout, README, screenshots, no large binaries.

lookFor: The brief asks to confirm the demo [stages into the VPK's installed library like the others](source:s1); the VPK bundles no example Deck Apps at all (only `runtime.js`, fonts and emoji), so the Vita build was checked for success only.

The brief names the package `demo`; the directory is `js/examples/demo` and the npm name follows the other examples (`@vitadeck/example-demo`), while the Deck App Package Name the CLI derives from "VitaDeck Demo" is `vitadeck-demo.vdapp`.
No `CMakeLists.txt` or `pnpm-workspace.yaml` change: both enumerate examples by glob (`examples/*`, `scripts/stage-example-apps.sh`).

groups.title: Example package and declared assets
groups.why: The demo is a package-shaped example like `smoke`, and the brief allows only a tiny committed image.
groups.summary: `vitadeck.config.json` declares the `mono` font and the `logo` image that the package files point at.
lookFor: Subtle: `assets/fonts/DejaVuSansMono.ttf` and its license are git symlinks to `../../../smoke/assets/fonts/`; the CLI's `copyFile` follows them, but a checkout without symlink support (Windows default) leaves a text file and the build fails on that font.
`logo.png` is a 302-byte 96×64 PNG generated by a throwaway script that is not committed.

groups.title: App frame and layout helpers
groups.why: Every section shares one frame and one way to place copy in a `Stack`.
groups.summary: `App.tsx` renders the active entry of `SECTIONS` inside a header, nav column and footer built from `Stack`s, and every section uses `Label`/`Section` from `ui.tsx`.
lookFor: `Label` wraps each `Text` in a transparent `Rect` because a `Stack` does not lay out `Text`; one `Text` per `Rect` also avoids the renderer stacking sibling `Text`s one line apart.
L and R wrap around through `step`; both `usePadButton` subscriptions live in `App`, so they work in every section, including Pad Buttons.

groups.title: Drawing and layout sections
groups.why: The brief lists Screen/theme/Rect, Text, Image, Stack and Scroll as sections.
groups.summary: Five stateless sections draw primitives and nest `Stack`s; `ScrollSection` holds its `Scroll` in a same-size `Rect` because a `Stack` does not lay out a `Scroll`.
lookFor: The Text section shows `한국어` as boxes on purpose and says so on screen, per the brief's note about #95.

groups.title: Input sections
groups.why: The brief asks for Button, Pad Button and TextInput behaviour with visible state.
groups.summary: Button, Pad Buttons and Text Input sections turn focus, press and pad events into on-screen state, and the Text Input writes its confirmed value to `storage`.
lookFor: `ButtonSection`'s `onBlur` resets the hint only if it still shows that Button's text, so the order of blur and focus events does not matter.
Each section with a primary Button sets `autoFocus`, so switching sections moves Focus out of the nav column into the section.

groups.title: Runtime API sections
groups.why: The brief asks for Storage, Timers, fetch and the Failure Screen.
groups.summary: Storage, Timers, fetch and Failure Screen sections use the Deck App globals, and `StorageSection` owns the `demo.counter`/`demo.name` keys the Text Input section imports.
lookFor: `FetchSection` requests `https://api.github.com/repos/matemolnar8/vitadeck` unauthenticated each time it mounts; GitHub allows 60 such requests per hour per IP, after which the error state shows `HTTP 403`.
`TimersSection` reads `getTime()` inside the interval callback, not during render, so the React Compiler cannot memoize a stale value.
Recovery text says to activate another Deck App and then the demo again, because the Shell does not restart a Deck App that is already active.

groups.title: README
groups.why: The brief asks for a README in the example and one line under "Start building".
groups.summary: The example README maps each section to its file and explains how to run it on the host and with `vitadeck dev`; the root README links it.

commits.subject: feat(examples): demo Deck App touring every SDK feature
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
One section per feature under src/sections/, composed by App.tsx with a nav column and L/R section switching. The Deck App Image is a 302-byte generated PNG; the mono font links the smoke example's copy.
